correctness.rationale: For r>1, fixed compactly supported positive environmental law µ with µ(ω>1)>0, Fermi mean-field sign is F_G(x)=r/G ∫(1+(ω−1)x)^(G−1)dµ−1. For each integer G>r, F_G(0)<0 and convexity (including the affine G=2 case) proves defection-only iff Q_G=F_G(1)+1≤1, otherwise exactly one interior unstable separatrix and two attracting boundary states. Hölder/Cauchy–Schwarz gives M_G²≤M_{G−1}M_{G+1}; division by G makes Q_G strictly log convex because (G²−1)/G²<1. A fixed positive mass above 1 makes Q_G→∞, so {G:Q_G≤1} is one finite contiguous integer interval or empty. For r=9/2, µ=(4/5)δ_(11/10)+(1/5)δ_(9/10), independently recomputed exact numerator differences at G=5,6,7,17,18: 86125,329277,−1440835,−29132543211735635,346187661271574877. Together with increasing adjacent Q ratios these prove complete G=5,6 bistability, 7..17 defection, G≥18 bistability. Exact independent rational binomial-moment checks were performed; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The monotonic-boundary question is natural for evolutionary public-goods games: it excludes any sequence of separated defection-only windows under a fixed environment, while an exact rational counterpoint demonstrates genuine loss and recovery of bistability. It is a useful structural theorem and a finite/all-integer phase classification, not a reformulation of one payoff calculation.

limitations: Fixed µ independent of G, compact positive support, positive mass ω>1, infinite-population mean-field Fermi dynamics; no finite-population fixation claim.
